subject: mathematics
question_text: If A, B, C, D are the angles of a cyclic quadrilateral, prove that (i) sin A − sin C = sin D − sin B and (ii) cos A + cos B + cos C + cos D = 0.

mark_split.label: Use A + C = π, B + D = π for (i)

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 29, book p.88. Both parts rest on the single cyclic-quadrilateral fact, so the 1 + 1 gives one mark to that fact together with part (i) and one to part (ii), where the sign change under π − θ has to be handled correctly four times. recall_prompt: Say how you would prove both parts — name the property of a cyclic quadrilateral you use, and what it does to sine and to cosine.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Use A + C = π, B + D = π for (i)
steps.margin_note: First mark. Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary. Pair A with C and B with D, never A with B. Then sin(π − θ) = sin θ finishes part (i).
steps.memory_tip: Opposite angles add to π, so pair A with C and B with D. Sine does not change under π − θ, so each difference in part (i) is zero.
lines: In a cyclic quadrilateral the opposite
A + C = π and B + D = π
(i) C = π − A ⇒ sin C = sin(π − A) = sin A
and D = π − B ⇒ sin D = sin B
∴ sin A − sin C = 0 = sin D − sin B

recall.must_convey: That opposite angles are supplementary, so sin C = sin A and sin D = sin B, making both sides of part (i) zero.
accept: opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to pi
C is pi minus A so sin C equals sin A
opposite angles supplementary, sin C ante sin A ye
sin of pi minus A is sin A so the difference is zero
reject: cos of pi minus A is minus cos A

steps.why: Every cyclic-quadrilateral proof uses one fact: opposite angles add to π. Once C = π − A is written, sin(π − A) = sin A finishes part (i) in a single move, and both sides turn out to be zero rather than merely equal.
common_mistakes: Pairing A with B instead of A with C.

steps.label: Reduce the four cosines for (ii)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Cosine flips sign under π − θ, so cos C = −cos A and cos D = −cos B, and the four terms cancel in two pairs.
steps.memory_tip: Under π − θ sine keeps its sign and cosine changes it. That one difference is why (i) gives zero on each side and (ii) cancels in pairs.
lines: and cos D = cos(π − B) = −cos B
cos A + cos B + cos C + cos D
= cos A + cos B − cos A − cos B

recall.must_convey: That cos C = −cos A and cos D = −cos B, so the four cosines cancel in two pairs and the sum is zero.
accept: cos of pi minus A is minus cos A so the terms cancel
cos C is minus cos A and cos D is minus cos B
the four cosines cancel in pairs giving zero

steps.why: Cosine changes sign under π − θ while sine does not. That single difference between the two reductions is why the sines in part (i) give zero on each side and the cosines in part (ii) cancel in two pairs.
common_mistakes: Writing cos(π − A) = cos A, which gives 2(cos A + cos B) instead of 0.
Using A + B = π in place of A + C = π.
